comparisons.note: an open miss, not a definitional difference: in wind hpr turns into the wind less than RocketPy (apogee drift -5.6%); flown once in calm air the codes agree to 1.3 to 3.7% (issue #50), so the gap is mostly the response to wind, which same-drag mode does not share (normal force, damping, drag at an angle). M2.1's landing offset is not met; reported, not scored, until #50 finds the cause.

an open miss, not a definitional difference: the landing point follows the apogee's (landing drift +7.0%); the horizontal path in wind is issue #50, and flown once in calm air the codes agree to 1.3 to 3.7%. M2.1's landing offset is not met; reported, not scored, until #50 finds the cause.

two peaks 0.9% apart in RocketPy: 111.18 m/s^2 on the rail at 0.05 s and 112.26 at 1.568 s, so its maximum is the later one; hpr's rail equation adds 1.16 m/s^2 of variable-mass terms at 0.05 s (thrust and mass equal to five digits), which lifts that peak to 112.35 and moves the maximum's time from one peak to the other. The size is gated.

the whole flight's maximum is the main parachute opening (191.8 m/s^2 in RocketPy, 351.1 in hpr, both at the instant the main opens), not a flight load; RocketPy counts the canopy's added mass (about 17 kg against the rocket's 20.8 kg) and hpr has none (ADR-012), which is a known difference in the opening, not in the flight. The power-on maximum is gated instead.
